seo.title: Fairmont Le Manoir Richelieu: Charlevoix Honeymoon Review
seo.description: Cliff-top castle hotel above the St Lawrence in La Malbaie. Score 85/100, from $400/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night plan.

content.verdict: Fairmont Le Manoir Richelieu is the original Charlevoix grand hotel — a Norman-château-style copper-roofed castle built in 1899 by Canada Steamship Lines on a cliff above the St Lawrence at La Malbaie, rebuilt after a 1928 fire, and now a 405-room Fairmont property that anchors the Charlevoix region the way the Château Frontenac anchors Old Quebec City. The setting is genuinely spectacular: the castle stands at the edge of a 200-foot cliff with panoramic views over the St Lawrence to the South Shore mountains; the championship Le Manoir Richelieu golf course (Robert Trent Jones-redesigned) wraps the property; the riverfront walk drops down to the historic boardwalk along the river. The G7 leaders’ summit happened here in 2018 — the entire hotel was taken over for security and infrastructure upgrades that left it in unusually good shape. The honeymoon proposition is the combination of Fairmont-Gold-level service, the Charlevoix landscape (mountains-meets-river, autumn foliage in late September to mid-October that rivals Vermont), the Casino de Charlevoix integrated into the property, and a serious spa (Le Manoir Spa) overlooking the river. Le Charlevoix restaurant is the formal dining room (Quebec farmhouse cuisine, sourcing from the region’s producers — Migneron, Hercule, Laiterie Charlevoix). The caveats: this is a large hotel (405 rooms) with conferences and groups; standard rooms without river view are less compelling than the Frontenac equivalent (Charlevoix is rural — the interior view is mostly woods, not a city panorama); and the autumn-foliage peak weeks book out 9–12 months ahead. But for couples whose Charlevoix honeymoon image is a cliff-top castle, river view, autumn maple foliage, golf, and spa — the Manoir Richelieu has no competition in the region. The honeymoon move is a Fairmont Gold Signature River View room or the Signature Suite, 3–4 nights paired with 3 nights in Old Quebec.
content.best_room: A Fairmont Gold Signature River View room (Gold floor concierge, private lounge, complimentary breakfast and evening canapés, river-facing window) is the honeymoon move. For a smaller budget, any Premier River View room without Gold. Avoid the standard interior rooms without river view — the view is the entire point.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Le Charlevoix dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive Quebec City (YQB) 1h 30min northeast to La Malbaie. Check-in to your Fairmont Gold River View, welcome cocktails. Dinner at Le Charlevoix.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Charlevoix foliage drive
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive Route 362 (the Route du Fleuve) — Baie-Saint-Paul, Les Éboulements, lunch at Le Mouton Noir. Afternoon at Domaine Forget concert (summer only). Spa evening.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Tadoussac and whale watching
itinerary_7_nights.description: 1h 30min drive northeast to Tadoussac — zodiac whale-watching boat (book in advance, May–Oct). Lunch at the Hôtel Tadoussac. Return for dinner in the Salle à Manger.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Golf or spa day
itinerary_7_nights.description: For golfers: round on the Manoir Richelieu course. For non-golfers: long morning at Le Manoir Spa — couples treatment, thermal pools overlooking the river. Lunch by the pool.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Cheese trail and Île aux Coudres
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive to Saint-Joseph-de-la-Rive — ferry to Île aux Coudres for the day. Lunch at La Mer Veille. Cheese tasting at Maison d’Affinage Maurice Dufour and Laiterie Charlevoix on return.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow castle day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning walk along the cliff promenade. Lunch on the terrace. Afternoon at the Casino de Charlevoix (within the hotel). Final dinner at Le Charlevoix.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast in the Gold Lounge, last cliff-edge walk, drive 1h 30min back to Quebec City.

caveats: Large hotel (405 rooms) with conference business. Fairmont Gold floor is the antidote — book it, don’t economise here.
Standard interior rooms without river view: avoid. The view is the entire reason to be here.
Foliage peak (late Sept to mid-Oct) books out 9–12 months ahead. Whale-watching at Tadoussac requires its own pre-booking.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Yes — particularly in late September to mid-October for foliage. The Fairmont Gold River View rooms are the honeymoon move.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: Late September to mid-October for foliage (the signature Charlevoix experience). June–August for warm weather and whale watching. December–February for winter castle atmosphere with skiing at Le Massif.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Foliage peak (late Sept–mid-Oct) Fairmont Gold rooms: 9–12 months ahead. June–August: 4–6 months. Other times: 2–3 months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No. Fairmont Gold floor is the closest you get to an adults-only experience.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Fairmont Gold Signature River View. For smaller budget, any Premier River View. Skip interior rooms.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Quebec City (YQB) is 1h 30min by car — the only practical entry. Train Charlevoix runs from Quebec City to La Malbaie seasonally (Jun–Oct, scenic route).
